# Verification

Checks that an email address belongs to whoever typed it, by a link sent to it. Contact asks for a
confirmation; this module sends the link, follows it and keeps the result. It is not an
account system and holds no messages. Sign-up does not use it: an account is verified by Payload's own
verify, in the [accounts note](/src/modules/accounts/README.md). In the CMS: the `email-confirmations` collection, whose token hash and send counters only the server writes; the hourly retention job is in the [jobs reference](/docs/reference/jobs.md). Fields, access and the confirm endpoint:
[email-confirmations content type](/docs/reference/content-types/email-confirmations.md); the
page's URL: [screens](/docs/reference/routes.md).

## How the pieces link

- The link's token is never stored: the record keeps its SHA-256, and a click finds the record again by that hash (`cms/token.ts`, `cms/store.ts`).
- Other modules never import this one. They call the service shaped by `src/platform/payload/emailConfirmer.ts`; `src/payload.config.ts` hands it over, with the `onConfirmed` listeners ([contact](/src/modules/contact/README.md)'s `markSubmissionsConfirmed`, which sends the held emails and marks messages confirmed) and the retention `keepers` (contact's `keepSendersWithMessages`, [accounts](/src/modules/accounts/README.md)' `keepAccountEmails`), decision 0008. The contract and the shared retention and error helpers are in the [shared Payload note](/src/platform/payload/README.md).
- Retention periods are in `src/platform/lib/retention.ts` (shared with contact); the link's 24 hours is `CONFIRMATION_LINK_LIFETIME_MS` in `src/platform/lib/linkLifetimes.ts`, used by `domain/limits.ts` and by the email's wording (`domain/emails.ts`).
- The per-address window (`sendCount`, `sendWindowStart`) and `tokenHash` are hidden and written only by the server (`cms/emailConfirmations.ts`, `domain/rules.ts`).
- `/confirm-email` (`src/app/(frontend)/confirm-email/page.tsx`) joins this module's button with [accounts](/src/modules/accounts/README.md)' `AccountOffer`, shown after confirming.

## Behaviors and events

- Opening the link changes nothing: the page only reads where the link stands (`use-cases/getConfirmationLinkStatus.ts`, #391) and hides the Confirm button for a used, expired or unknown link (`ui/ConfirmEmail.client.tsx`).
- The Confirm button posts the token with the robot check (Turnstile, decision 0003), because mail scanners open links and some run scripts (`cms/confirmEndpoint.ts`, #303). When the check is on (it runs only while the verifier is enabled), nothing is confirmed without a passing one.
- The first valid click within 24 hours confirms, runs every listener, then sends the welcome email. One failing listener, or a failed welcome, is logged and stops nothing; a later click answers `already-confirmed` (`cms/confirmEmail.ts`, `domain/rules.ts`).
- Confirming is one conditional write, so two clicks at once confirm once. It also sets `welcomeSentAt` before the send: the welcome goes at most once and is never retried (`cms/store.ts` `markConfirmed`).
- A request sends a link only within the limits below; a new link replaces the old one, so only the newest works. The record is saved before the email goes out (`cms/requestConfirmation.ts`).
- An address already confirmed gets no new link; something that isn't one address gets nothing (`cms/requestConfirmation.ts`).
- The service never throws: an unknown state counts as unconfirmed and a failure is logged, so the message or sign-up that asked is never lost. It works in its own transaction, so a failure can't roll back the caller's (`cms/emailConfirmer.ts`, `cms/ownTransaction.ts`).
- Payload's email check is stricter than the site's, so an address it refuses gets no record and no link; the asking message stays, unconfirmed (`cms/emailConfirmations.ts`).
- Retention, hourly (`cms/retention.ts`): an unconfirmed address goes 48 hours after its last link; a confirmed one 12 months after it was confirmed, unless a keeper still needs it. A failing keeper stops the run before anything confirmed is deleted. Deletes re-check their conditions, so a fresh link or confirmation in between survives (`cms/store.ts`).
- Logs carry only the kind of failure, never an address; the retention log has counts only (`cms/logFailure.ts`, `cms/retention.ts`).

## Shared pieces it uses

- `SlidingWindowCounter`, `parseEmailAddress`, `parseClientIp`, `toEmailHtml`, retention cutoffs (`src/platform/lib/`); the robot check (`src/platform/lib/humanCheck`, `src/platform/turnstile/`); the jobs schedule (`src/platform/payload/retentionJobs.ts`); `PageHeader`, `Section` on the page.

## Rules and the tests that protect them

- **Only the hash of a link's token is kept.** Tokens are 32 random bytes (43 characters), so a leaked database cannot be replayed (`cms/token.ts`; `cms/token.test.ts`).
- **A link is sent only within three limits:** 5 an hour per connection, 3 a day per address, 30 an hour site-wide. Over any, nothing is sent, the person's answer is the same and the reason goes to the log; a new link replaces the old; a confirmed address gets none. Counters are in memory (one process), and with no client IP only the site-wide one applies (`domain/limits.ts`, `domain/rules.ts`; `cms/requestConfirmation.test.ts`, `domain/rules.test.ts`).
- **A click confirms once, within 24 hours.** It needs the robot check (while the verifier is on), is one conditional write, runs every listener, then sends the welcome email at most once; a failing listener or welcome is logged and stops nothing. Confirm clicks are limited to 20 an hour per connection, then a 429 (`cms/confirmEmail.ts`, `cms/confirmEndpoint.ts`; `cms/confirmEmail.test.ts`, `cms/confirmEndpoint.test.ts`).
- **Only a real address gets a record and a link:** something that is not one address gets nothing, and Payload's email check is stricter than the site's, so an address it refuses gets no record and no link while the asking message stays, unconfirmed; a later click on a used link answers `already-confirmed` (`cms/requestConfirmation.ts`, `cms/emailConfirmations.ts`, `cms/confirmEmail.ts`; `cms/requestConfirmation.test.ts`).
- **Asking never loses the caller's work.** The service never throws, an unknown state counts as unconfirmed, and it runs in its own transaction (`cms/emailConfirmer.ts`; `cms/emailConfirmer.test.ts`, `cms/ownTransaction.test.ts`).
- **Retention keeps what is still needed.** Hourly: an unconfirmed address goes 48 hours after its last link; a confirmed one 12 months after confirmation, unless a keeper (a kept message, an account) still needs it. A failing keeper stops the run before a confirmed address is deleted, and each delete re-checks its conditions (`cms/retention.ts`; `cms/retention.test.ts`).
- **Opening the link changes nothing,** so a mail scanner confirms nothing; the button hides for a used, expired or unknown link (`use-cases/getConfirmationLinkStatus.ts`, `ui/ConfirmEmail.client.tsx`; `use-cases/getConfirmationLinkStatus.test.ts`, `ui/ConfirmEmail.client.test.tsx`).
- **Logs carry the kind of failure, never an address** (`cms/logFailure.ts`); email text and link: `domain/emails.test.ts`. Contact gets the confirmer and its listener: `src/payload.config.confirmation.test.ts`.

## Boundaries

- Entries: `index.ts` (types, pure rules), `server.ts` (page component, status use case), `cms.ts` (collection, service, retention task; never server-only). It imports no other module; lint enforces it.
